question.prompt: The sum of three numbers is \(98.\) The ratio of the first to the second is \(\dfrac23,\) and the ratio of the second to the third is \(\dfrac58.\) The second number is:

solutions.explanation:
Both given ratios involve the second number, so represent that number by the same number of parts in each ratio. Scale \(2:3\) to \(10:15\), and scale \(5:8\) to \(15:24\). This gives
\[
\text{first}:\text{second}:\text{third}=10:15:24.
\]
There are \(10+15+24=49\) parts altogether. Their sum is \(98\), so each part is \(98/49=2\). The second number is therefore \(15\cdot2=30\), choice C.
solutions.title: Match the shared ratio term
